dataset_source.title: Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds
dataset_source.attribution: Source data: Tiago F. T. Cerqueira, Antonio Sanna and Miguel A. L. Marques, Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds, Materials Cloud 2023.163 v1, DOI 10.24435/materialscloud:qv-bq, CC BY 4.0. This catalogue is a derived projection with additional source-state screening commentary.

scope: Previously private source-model screening is now published as unscored source-computed material-design hypotheses. Historical private-screening wording is retained as context. These predictions are new to this reviewed catalogue only; experimental confirmation, worldwide first discovery, formal RPS and human scientific review are not claimed.
source_tc_scope: Source isotropic Eliashberg Tc in K at mu*=0.1 is a model result, not experimental Tc. It is a separate source product and is not associated with an individual Gaussian width or a numerical uncertainty interval.
pairing_response_scope: Retained ten-width lambda contrasts and independent source Tc products support bounded source-model comparisons. Chemical, mass, volume, sampling, spin and SOC effects can co-change; no universal causal or error-bound interpretation is assigned.
risk_tag_scope: Attention labels support browsing. Element labels are not measured magnetic ground states, rejection criteria or calibrated potential scores; no label does not mean no risk.

candidate.prototype: P4/mmm ordered five-site tetragonal hydride: H corner, Ru c-axis midpoint, Mo body center, two Tc basal edge centers
candidate.prototype_evidence: P4/mmm ordered five-site tetragonal hydride: H corner, Ru c-axis midpoint, Mo body center, two Tc basal edge centers
candidate.support_meaning: Preliminary screened support within the stated source model. This ordinal level is not a probability, formal RPS score or human scientific review.
candidate.risk_summary: The actual source target has no negative sampled-path value and positive Gamma optical compression. Fine stress reaches 0.459 GPa although forces vanish by symmetry, so cell response remains a concrete next test. Hydrogen desorption/decomposition, cation disorder, Tc/Ru phase competition and SOC can change the result; radioactivity is a practical limitation, not fabricated evidence of phonon instability. No exact thermodynamic equilibrium or experimental realization is claimed.
candidate.ambient_scope: Both source SCFs converge, near-zero coarse forces/stress and bounded fine response are measured. Fine Fmax=0 eV/A, P=0.009 GPa, full max stress=0.459 GPa. Gamma optical compression is positive beyond printing bound and sampled path has no signed negative values. All listed q outputs have JOBDONE/last response convergence and no routine errors. This supports a finite-grid local/metastable source model, not global hull or experimental synthesis.
candidate.route_response: Mo replaces W on the unique body-centered metal site with H, Ru and two Tc roles retained. Volume contracts 0.5125%, Mo-Ru versus W-Ru falls 0.0046193 A and H-Mo versus H-W falls 0.0057705 A. All ten lambda values rise 14.206–21.248%, with separate Eli mu=.1 11.976 to 15.603 K. The effect is a measured coupled site/network construction, not a nominal-valence or DOS carrier inference.
candidate.next_action: At the frozen Mo/W site roles compare common volume and electronic/q sampling, then test the dominant H-loss or cation-disorder competitor and residual-cell strain. Stable persistent coupling gain supports the screen; a nontranslation unstable branch, low-energy decomposition or lost paired gain opposes it.

seven_criteria.identity: Complete ordered CIF/literal coarse-fine input/Gamma periodic species-site association is numerically supported; source input geometry and full tensor/forces are retained. Export occupancy is a discrete computational convention; source experimental P/T/occupancy and actual compiled unit constant are unknown. Exact-version input defaults scope the configured neutral scalar spin1/noSOC model, not magnetic ground state.
seven_criteria.quantitative_route_response: Mo replaces W on the unique body-centered metal site with H, Ru and two Tc roles retained. Volume contracts 0.5125%, Mo-Ru versus W-Ru falls 0.0046193 A and H-Mo versus H-W falls 0.0057705 A. All ten lambda values rise 14.206–21.248%, with separate Eli mu=.1 11.976 to 15.603 K. The effect is a measured coupled site/network construction, not a nominal-valence or DOS carrier inference.
seven_criteria.pairing_relevance: Exact target and mapped control direct source lambda arrays have the same favorable sign at all ten common broadening tokens; omega_ln has explicit K units and separate Eli/McM mu=.1 tables remain independent. Same underlying q mesh is observed. The sensitivity range is not a physical error bound; sigma units, full-BZ convergence, experimental Tc and pure-geometry causality remain unknown. Literal method differences are declared confounds.
seven_criteria.ambient_feasibility: Both source SCFs converge, near-zero coarse forces/stress and bounded fine response are measured. Fine Fmax=0 eV/A, P=0.009 GPa, full max stress=0.459 GPa. This supports a finite-grid local/metastable source model, not global hull or experimental synthesis.
seven_criteria.competition_and_coherence: The actual source target has no negative sampled-path value and positive Gamma optical compression. Hydrogen desorption/decomposition, cation disorder, Tc/Ru phase competition and SOC can change the result; radioactivity is a practical limitation, not fabricated evidence of phonon instability. seven_criteria.novelty: Dated 2026-10-07 exact MoTc2RuH/HMoTc2Ru superconductivity queries identified no experimental exact-phase benchmark. The MC2023 predicted phase is acknowledged prior. Novelty is this bounded Mo-for-W ordered hydride construction in the reviewed catalogue, not a first composition claim.
